entity.name: Soham Mitra
entity.description: Independent developer in Mumbai, India, building Vlocalhost AI: a meeting recorder that records, transcribes and summarises entirely on the user's own machine. No audio, transcript or note is uploaded anywhere, there is no account and no backend, and the core is AGPL-3.0 with the source public so the part that touches your audio can be read and verified. Built for people who cannot send a meeting to a cloud at all.

projects.name: Vlocalhost Core
projects.description: An on-device meeting notetaker for Windows and macOS. Audio is captured locally, transcribed with faster-whisper on the endpoint, and summarised by a local model the user chooses; the transcript is written to disk before the summary is attempted, so a missing model never costs you the meeting. Notes are Markdown and plain text in a folder you pick, not rows in a database. There is no telemetry, no crash reporting and no analytics, because there is no endpoint to send them to. The app is also an MCP server, so an assistant such as Claude or Cursor can start a recording, follow the live transcript and search your own notes without any of it leaving the machine. Every release publishes a SHA-256 for each file and a GitHub build attestation, so the bytes you downloaded can be checked against the bytes that were built.

channels.description: Grants and sponsorship are arranged directly by email at voiceit@vlocal.host. No public payment endpoint is published yet; one will be added here when it exists rather than listed speculatively.

plans.name: Code signing and notarization (floor: 1 of 2)
plans.description: Windows builds are unsigned and macOS builds ad-hoc signed, not notarized, so both operating systems warn the app cannot be verified. For a tool asking to be trusted with confidential meetings, that first-run warning does real damage. Covers an Apple Developer membership, a Windows certificate with the hardware token now required, and the signing pipeline. Until funded, every release publishes a SHA-256 per file and a GitHub build attestation. USD 1,200 of the USD 10,000 floor.

plans.name: Indian-language transcription: corpus and benchmark (floor: 2 of 2)
plans.description: Built in India, the project still cannot claim Indian-language support: Whisper is weak on Indic speech and code-mixing, and nobody has measured how weak. Open-weight Indic models exist and the app already supports bringing your own, so this is measurement, not architecture. Funds recording and licensing real multi-speaker meeting audio with consent and fair payment to speakers, compute to score models, and publishing every result. USD 8,800 of the USD 10,000 floor.

plans.name: Scaling and testing -- the full programme (ceiling)
plans.description: The full programme, itemised. Engineering time USD 44,000: a year of focused work on what a teardown against three rival products showed matters most, being native-format audio capture, on-device diarization, encryption at rest and Indic models. Device lab USD 18,000. Indian-language corpus USD 18,000. Independent audit of the no-egress claim, published in full, USD 8,000. Cross-platform CI USD 7,000. Accessibility USD 5,000. Any subset can be funded.

plans.name: Ongoing maintenance and support
plans.description: Keeping the recorder working across Windows and macOS updates, audio-device changes and model releases, answering issues, and keeping the dependency set pinned, audited and reflected in the published SBOM. Any amount. The ask in this manifest is a range: a USD 10,000 floor (the two one-time plans above) to a USD 100,000 ceiling (the full programme).
